text:
maria: Heads-up, seeing ~6 nodes in gpu-pool-us-west1 flip to NotReady/NoSchedule over the last 10m. GPU pods stuck Pending because kubelet tainted the nodes. device-plugin pods are OOMKilled in a loop on the affected nodes.

devon: ack. Any recent driver or node image changes rolled?

maria: Not that I can see in release history. Kernel logs show repeated oom_reaper / cgroup memory kills targeted at nvidia device-plugin. Suspect a memory leak under driver 535.x + our ds config.

akash: Can you paste the pod status and a log snippet?

maria: ``kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide | grep nvidia-device-plugin`` shows CrashLoopBackOff on nodes gpu-usw1-*-preempt. Logs: ``OOMKilled: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError?`` (weird), full log: ``kubelet: memory cgroup out of memory: kill process 12345 (nvidia-device-plugin) score 999``

julia: weird that it's Java in our ds, must be a wrapper process for metrics exporter. Either way OOMs mean requests/limits too low or node under memory pressure. Are these preemptible nodes?

maria: yes most are preemptible; pool autoscaled fast last night. autoscaler bot: ``cluster-autoscaler-bot: Scaling activity: gpu-pool-us-west1 decreased from 12 to 6 (scale-down).`` We probably hit a compaction/GC pattern causing memory spike.

cluster-autoscaler-bot: Note: nodes in NotReady state will not be replaced until they are confirmed unhealthy for >10m by cloud provider health checks.

devon: Meanwhile CA can't add new capacity because max for that pool is 20 and we're not hitting quota, but autoscaler won't create until taints cleared or pods evicted. Any pods pinned to those nodes?

maria: Some stateful local-storage pods pinned. Also kubelet tainted with node.kubernetes.io/not-ready:NoSchedule when device-plugin fails. So Pending GPU workload piles up.

akash: Quick mitigation options: 1) increase device-plugin memory requests/limits in the DaemonSet, 2) restart device-plugin with init container that trims caches, 3) temporarily cordon/force-delete pods on sick nodes to let autoscaler create replacements, 4) drain and reprovision nodes as non-preemptible for the hot window.

julia: +1 to bumping requests. We should also add an eviction threshold change: set kubelet --system-reserved and kube-reserved to give device-plugin headroom. Also disable swap if any nodes have it (swap can make OOM behavior weird).

maria: Trying a focused test: bumped mem limit from 200Mi -> 1Gi on staging device-plugin DS and rolled on one node. Will monitor.

k8s-bot: kubelet on gpu-usw1-03: ``Eviction manager: attempted to reclaim memory``; ``device-plugin container restarted 6 times``

jc: If bump resolves, we should ship a canary patch to prod DS across one AZ at a time. Also add liveness probe to avoid stuck containers hogging memory?

devon: Also check driver version; if driver 535.x is root cause we may need to pin to 530.x temporarily while we work with NVIDIA. That has infra cost (reinstall, node reboot). Tradeoff: stability vs churn.

maria: For immediate triage I will: 1) cordon two worst nodes, 2) kubectl delete pods nvidia-device-plugin on them to trigger replacement on remaining nodes, 3) bump DS mem request in a canary. If that looks good, we'll roll.

akash: When you cordon, remember cluster-autoscaler won't add nodes if pods are unschedulable due to taint. Force-deleting the GPU pods is fine if they are stateless. Watch for local SSD stuck pods.

maria: Cordon + force-delete done on gpu-usw1-03 and -07. Cluster-autoscaler notified: ``scale-up: 2 nodes requested for pending gpu workloads``

cluster-autoscaler-bot: Scaling up: requesting 2 nodes in gpu-pool-us-west1 (provisioning)… ETA ~2m

julia: Good. If we see memory pressure persist on new nodes, we should consider adding a verticalPodAutoscaler or set down the preemptible percentage for this pool to avoid mass reclaim during spikes. Cost vs availability tradeoff to discuss.

maria: Canary bump applied to DS on one AZ. Device-plugin stayed up for 12m so far vs immediate OOM previously. Rolling to remaining AZs now.

devon: After roll, open an infra ticket to: pin driver version, increase device-plugin mem, add kube-reserved and system-reserved changes, and add a monitor alert for device-plugin OOMs. Also add docs on draining GPU nodes that carry local state.

julia: FYI I already sat with NVIDIA support earlier today; they acknowledged a leak in 535.2 for our distro. They recommended the mem bump as temporary workaround and working on a patch. If true, we'll plan a rolling driver upgrade once fixed.

maria: Post-mortem action items I will create: "gpu-deviceplugin-memory-bump", "kubelet-reserved-tuning", "ticket-nvidia-driver-535-leak".

akash: Thanks. Also consider setting the device-plugin DS to use hostPID and hostNetwork only if required — prefer cgroups isolation instead.

maria: Noted. Will track in infra board. For now scaling recovered and Pending GPU queue drained. Closing thread once I file tickets. :white_check_mark:
